note: SEA PLACES — named locations in open water a fleet can sail to and arrive at. AUTHORED, deliberately: unlike the 214 harbours these are not settlements with a Wikidata item apiece, they are waters a sailor of 1550 knew by name — a bank, a strait, a belt of wind. Coordinates are placed by hand where the named water actually is, and scripts/build-sea-places.mjs REFUSES any point that is not sea on the same 0.25 degree raster the leg graph is derived from, so a place on land cannot reach the chain. The spur legs joining each place to its nearest harbours are GENERATED (sailed A* water distances, same rule as data/sea-routes.json) — run the script again after editing this file.

places.name: Cape St Vincent
places.approach: The cape every Lisbon sailing rounds; the sea road south turns east here, and half the shipping of Iberia passes within sight of the cliff.

places.name: Strait of Gibraltar
places.approach: The Pillars of Hercules: eight miles of water between two continents, and everything that enters or leaves the Middle Sea comes through it.

places.name: Bay of Biscay
places.approach: The graveyard of the Atlantic coast: a westerly gale piles the whole ocean into this bight, and a ship caught on that lee shore claws off it or does not.

places.name: Dogger Bank
places.approach: A drowned country in the middle of the North Sea, ten fathoms down. The cod ground of Europe; the doggers fish it in every season the weather allows.

places.name: The Grand Banks
places.approach: Fog, ice, and cod beyond counting. The Basques and Bretons crossed an ocean for these shallows before any crown had mapped them.

places.name: The Sargasso Sea
places.approach: A sea with no shore, marked only by its weed. The gulfweed rafts stretch to every horizon, and sailors swear becalmed ships have grown into it.

places.name: The Horse Latitudes
places.approach: The belt of calms at thirty north, where the trade winds die. Ships have lain here for weeks; the name is said to come from what thirst made the crews throw overboard.

places.name: The Doldrums
places.approach: The dead belt on the line, between the trades of two hemispheres. Glassy calm, thunder squalls, and the daily creep of the current setting you back the way you came.

places.name: The Skeleton Coast
places.approach: A desert shore of fog and surf, littered with the ribs of ships and whales. The Portuguese called it the Gates of Hell: a landing here is easy, and leaving is not.

places.name: The Roaring Forties
places.approach: Run your easting down: below forty south the west wind never stops, and a ship bound for the Indies rides it like a cart downhill — if her gear holds.

places.name: Drake Passage
places.approach: The worst water on earth, south of the Horn, where two oceans meet with nothing to break them. Greybeard seas, snow in midsummer, and no shelter for a thousand miles.

places.name: Bab-el-Mandeb
places.approach: The Gate of Tears, where the Red Sea narrows to a musket-shot of water. Every hull between Suez and the Indies threads it, and everyone on both shores knows that.

places.name: Strait of Hormuz
places.approach: The neck of the Gulf, commanded by the barren island whose customs house grew rich on it. If the world were a ring, they said, Hormuz would be the jewel in it.

places.name: One Fathom Bank
places.approach: The shoal narrows of the Malacca strait, where the deep channel runs a cable wide between mudbanks. Every monsoon fleet between India and China files through in single line.
